name: sidebar-atlas
description: Atlas brand vertical nav rail ("NavBar" in Figma). A 70px-wide, full-height vertical stack: a top logo slot followed by ten navbar-item entries (Search, Map, Home, Todo, Benchmark, Matching, Operations, Contracts, Reporting, Admin). Plain COMPONENT with no variants — Figma models interaction states one level down, inside each navbar-item instance, not on the rail itself. TODO: radixPrimitive is a best guess (NavigationMenu.Root) since this is a static content-navigation landmark, not a Radix-primitive-driven widget; confirm during adaptation whether a bare <nav> is preferable to importing @radix-ui/react-navigation-menu.

anatomy.notes: 70px-wide vertical flex stack (flex-col items-center), no wrapper frame around the nav items — logo and all ten navbar-item instances are DIRECT children of root, in document order. paddingTop/paddingBottom 24px, no horizontal padding, itemSpacing 16px between every child (logo-to-first-item and item-to-item alike). Sized FIXED 70x800 in Figma; the 800px height is a canvas sample only — the rail is meant to stretch to its container's full height (adapter should use h-full / min-h-screen, not a fixed 800px).

RECTANGLE 'image 12', 48x51, IMAGE fill (Atlas logo artwork, imageHash 90cdf662b547c2a8ac07862b5aa4b64de2efac75, scaleMode FILL). Not an INSTANCE — no klp equivalent exists or is expected; image fills cannot bind to a Figma variable, so there is nothing to flag as a token gap here. Adapter should expose this as a consumer-provided slot (e.g. a `logo` prop defaulting to a minimal placeholder mark), not a hardcoded asset import.

a11y.notes: This is a primary navigation landmark. Root should render as <nav aria-label="Primary"> (or similar), with each nav-item rendered as <a> (navbar-item is asChild-friendly per its own spec) carrying aria-current="page" when it represents the active route. The logo slot at top should be either decorative (aria-hidden, if a home link exists elsewhere) or itself a link to the app root with descriptive alt text — the adapter must decide based on how the consumer wires routing. All ten items are State=default in this capture; hover/selected visuals are owned entirely by navbar-item's own state machine (see .klp/figma-refs/navbar-item/spec.json) and must remain reachable via :focus-visible for keyboard users, not just :hover.

tokenGaps.note: Root fill is the literal #22222D, bound to no variable anywhere in the file (confirmed exhaustively across every collection). A DS-side alias --klp-bg-navrail was added pointing at the nearest existing primitive storm-900 (#191D2C, RGB distance 10, imperceptible). Figma should introduce a real token for this nav-rail surface so the alias can point at an authoritative source instead of an approximation.
